Restated before interest: ABBV paid $3,002mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2025, 4.91% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Restated at replacement capex: ABBV spent $1,214mm on plant over 2025 against $762mm of plant depreciation, 0.74% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 32.46% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2025 supports 38.40%, so the charge rebuilds at -5.94%. It was held at nil, but ABBV books $7,377mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside cost of sales in FY2025 (0001551152-26-000008), 12.06% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -5.94%. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -5.94% to -7.35%.

column11: ANCHOR, the measured use of preoperative botulinum toxin in complex repairs today: at Carolinas Medical Center 11.0% of open abdominal wall reconstructions in 2023 to 2024 received it, up from 2.9% in 2016 to 2017, while component separation fell from 48.0% to 19.9% (Kerr SW et al., Am J Surg 2026;256:116919, 1,484 patients). MULTIPLE 1.0, A JUDGEMENT: 11.0% x 1.0. For more: a label and AbbVie's promotion would carry the practice beyond the centres that built it. Against: Carolinas publishes much of the US experience with the technique (Deerenberg 2021, Kerr 2026, and the nationwide analysis by Ayuso et al., Surgery 2022), so national off-label use today is likely lower; a meta-analysis of six propensity-matched studies (851 patients) found no significant effect on fascial closure or component separation (Preoperative botulinum toxin for complex abdominal wall reconstruction, springermedicine.com); and off-label Botox stays available at the same course price
